title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
description:
Given a string s, find the length of the longest contiguous substring that contains no repeated character.

Example: in abcabcbb the answer is 3 (abc).

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ |s| ≤ 15000
  • s contains only lowercase letters and digits

Input

A single line containing s.

Output

A single integer: the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.

title: Group the Anagrams
description:
Given a list of words, group together the words that are anagrams of each other (same letters, possibly in a different order).

Inside each group, sort the words lexicographically (identical words are kept, each occurrence counts). Then print the groups ordered by their first (smallest) word.

Input:
6
eat tea tan ate nat bat

Output:
ate eat tea
bat
nat tan

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 1000
  • Each word has 1 to 10 lowercase letters

Input

  • Line 1: an integer n
  • Line 2: n words separated by single spaces

Output

One group per line, the words of a group separated by single spaces.

6
eat tea tan ate nat bat

ate eat tea
bat
nat tan

title: Roman to Integer
description:
Convert a Roman numeral to an integer. The symbols are I=1, V=5, X=10, L=50, C=100, D=500, M=1000. When a smaller symbol appears before a larger one it is subtracted (IV=4, IX=9, XL=40, XC=90, CD=400, CM=900).

Constraints

  • The numeral is valid and represents a value from 1 to 3999

Input

A single line containing the Roman numeral in uppercase.

Output

The integer value.

title: Integer to Roman
description:
Convert an integer to a Roman numeral using the standard subtractive form: M=1000, CM=900, D=500, CD=400, C=100, XC=90, L=50, XL=40, X=10, IX=9, V=5, IV=4, I=1.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 3999

Input

A single integer n.

Output

The Roman numeral in uppercase.

title: Zigzag Conversion
description:
Write the string s in a zigzag pattern on r rows (go down the rows, then diagonally back up, and repeat), then read it row by row.

For PAYPALISHIRING with 3 rows:

P   A   H   N
A P L S I I G
Y   I   R

Reading row by row gives PAHNAPLSIIGYIR.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ |s| ≤ 1000
  • 1 ≤ r ≤ 1000
  • s contains letters, digits, , and . only

Input

  • Line 1: the string s
  • Line 2: the number of rows r

Output

The converted string.

title: Longest Common Prefix
description:
Find the longest string that is a prefix of every word in the list.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 200
  • Each word has 1 to 200 lowercase letters

Input

  • Line 1: an integer n
  • Line 2: n words separated by single spaces

Output

The longest common prefix, or NONE if it is empty.
solution:
n = int(input())
w = input().split()
p = w[0]
for x in w[1:]:
    while not x.startswith(p):
        p = p[:-1]
print(p if p else "NONE")

title: String Rotation Check
description:
A string b is a rotation of a if it can be obtained by moving some characters from the front of a to its back (e.g. erbottlewat is a rotation of waterbottle). A string is a rotation of itself.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ |a|, |b| ≤ 5000
  • Both strings contain only lowercase letters

Input

  • Line 1: string a
  • Line 2: string b

Output

YES if b is a rotation of a, otherwise NO.
solution:
a = input().strip()
b = input().strip()
print("YES" if len(a) == len(b) and b in a + a else "NO")

title: Isomorphic Strings
description:
Two strings are isomorphic if the characters of the first can be replaced to get the second, where every occurrence of a character is replaced by the same character and no two different characters map to the same character. A character may map to itself.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ |s|, |t| ≤ 10000
  • Both strings contain only lowercase letters and digits

Input

  • Line 1: string s
  • Line 2: string t

Output

YES if they are isomorphic, otherwise NO (strings of different lengths are never isomorphic).

title: Longest Palindromic Substring
description:
Find the longest contiguous substring of s that reads the same forwards and backwards. If several have the maximum length, print the one that starts leftmost.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ |s| ≤ 10000
  • s contains only lowercase letters
  • An O(n3) brute force is too slow

Input

A single line containing s.

Output

The longest palindromic substring.

title: Minimum Window Substring
description:
Given strings s and t, find the shortest contiguous substring of s that contains every character of t (including duplicates: if t has two a's, the window needs at least two). If several shortest windows exist, print the leftmost one.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ |s|, |t| ≤ 15000
  • Strings contain only letters (case-sensitive)
  • An O(n2) approach is too slow; use a sliding window

Input

  • Line 1: string s
  • Line 2: string t

Output

The minimum window, or NONE if no window exists.

title: Decode the Nested String
description:
A string is encoded with the rule k[text], meaning text is repeated exactly k times. Encodings can be nested and concatenated. Decode the string.

Examples: 3[a]2[bc] → aaabcbc, 3[a2[c]] → accaccacc.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ |s| ≤ 100
  • s is valid: digits appear only as repeat counts k (1 ≤ k ≤ 300), brackets are balanced
  • Letters are lowercase
  • The decoded string has at most 10000 characters

Input

A single line containing the encoded string.

Output

The decoded string.

title: Restore IP Addresses
description:
A valid IPv4 address consists of exactly four numbers (each from 0 to 255) separated by dots, and no number has leading zeros (0 is fine, 01 is not). Given a string of digits, find all valid IP addresses that can be formed by inserting three dots into it (without reordering or removing digits).

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ |s| ≤ 20
  • s contains only digits

Input

A single line containing the digit string s.

Output

All valid addresses, one per line, sorted in ascending lexicographic (string) order. If there are none, print NONE.

title: Pattern Occurrences (KMP)
description:
Find every position where pattern p occurs in text t. Occurrences may overlap. Positions are 0-based.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ |p| ≤ |t| ≤ 15000 (or |p| > |t|, in which case there are no occurrences)
  • Strings contain only lowercase letters
  • A naive O(|t|·|p|) comparison may be too slow; use KMP or the Z-algorithm

Input

  • Line 1: the text t
  • Line 2: the pattern p

Output

Line 1: the number of occurrences. If it is greater than 0, line 2: the starting positions in increasing order, separated by single spaces.

title: Text Justification
description:
Format the words into lines of exactly W characters, fully justified:

  • Pack as many words as possible into each line (greedily), with at least one space between words.
  • Distribute the extra spaces as evenly as possible between words; if they do not divide evenly, the gaps on the left get more spaces than the gaps on the right.
  • A line with a single word is left-justified (padded with spaces on the right).
  • The last line is left-justified: words separated by single spaces, padded with spaces on the right.

So that the padding is visible, print each line between two | characters.

Input:
16
This is an example of text justification.

Output:
|This    is    an|
|example  of text|
|justification.  |

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ W ≤ 100
  • 1 ≤ number of words ≤ 300
  • Each word has between 1 and W non-space characters

Input

  • Line 1: the width W
  • Line 2: the words separated by single spaces

Output

The justified lines, each in the form |line| where line has exactly W characters.
solution:
W = int(input())
words = input().split()
lines = []
i = 0
while i < len(words):
    j, length = i, 0
    while j < len(words) and length + len(words[j]) + (j - i) <= W:
        length += len(words[j])
        j += 1
    line = words[i:j]
    if j == len(words) or len(line) == 1:
        s = ' '.join(line)
        s += ' ' * (W - len(s))
    else:
        gaps = len(line) - 1
        spaces = W - length
        q, r = divmod(spaces, gaps)
        s = ''
        for k, w in enumerate(line[:-1]):
            s += w + ' ' * (q + (1 if k < r else 0))
        s += line[-1]
    lines.append('|' + s + '|')
    i = j
print('\n'.join(lines))

title: Add Big Numbers as Strings
description:
Add two very large non-negative integers given as strings. You must not convert the whole strings to integers with int(); add them digit by digit like you would on paper.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ length of each number ≤ 5000
  • Numbers have no leading zeros (except the number 0 itself)

Input

  • Line 1: the first number a
  • Line 2: the second number b

Output

The sum a + b without leading zeros.
solution:
a = input().strip()
b = input().strip()
i, j, carry = len(a) - 1, len(b) - 1, 0
res = []
while i >= 0 or j >= 0 or carry:
    d = carry
    if i >= 0:
        d += ord(a[i]) - 48
        i -= 1
    if j >= 0:
        d += ord(b[j]) - 48
        j -= 1
    res.append(chr(d % 10 + 48))
    carry = d // 10
print(''.join(reversed(res)))

title: Smallest Lexicographic Rotation
description:
Among all rotations of string s (rotation k is s[k:] + s[:k]), find the lexicographically smallest one. If several values of k give the same smallest rotation, choose the smallest k.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ |s| ≤ 15000
  • s contains only lowercase letters
  • Comparing all n rotations naively is O(n2) and too slow; aim for O(n) (e.g. the minimum-expression two-pointer method or Booth's algorithm)

Input

A single line containing s.

Output

Line 1: the index k. Line 2: the smallest rotation.
solution:
s = input().strip()
n = len(s)
i, j, k = 0, 1, 0
while i < n and j < n and k < n:
    a = s[(i + k) % n]
    b = s[(j + k) % n]
    if a == b:
        k += 1
        continue
    if a > b:
        i += k + 1
    else:
        j += k + 1
    if i == j:
        j += 1
    k = 0
p = min(i, j)
print(p)
print(s[p:] + s[:p])

title: Shortest Palindrome by Prepending
description:
You may add characters only to the front of string s. Find the shortest palindrome you can make this way.

Example: abcd → dcbabcd, aacecaaa → aaacecaaa.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ |s| ≤ 8000
  • s contains only lowercase letters
  • Checking every prefix for being a palindrome is O(n2); use the KMP failure function for O(n)

Input

A single line containing s.

Output

The shortest palindrome.
solution:
s = input().strip()
t = s + '#' + s[::-1]
f = [0] * len(t)
k = 0
for i in range(1, len(t)):
    while k and t[i] != t[k]:
        k = f[k - 1]
    if t[i] == t[k]:
        k += 1
    f[i] = k
print(s[f[-1]:][::-1] + s)

title: Wildcard Matching
description:
Decide whether the pattern p matches the entire string s, where:

  • ? matches any single character;
  • * matches any sequence of characters (including the empty sequence);
  • any other character matches only itself.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ |s|, |p| ≤ 1000
  • s contains lowercase letters; p contains lowercase letters, ? and *
  • Plain backtracking is exponential on patterns with many *; use dynamic programming or the greedy star-backtrack method

Input

  • Line 1: the string s
  • Line 2: the pattern p

Output

YES if the pattern matches the whole string, otherwise NO.
solution:
s = input().strip()
p = input().strip()
i = j = 0
star = -1
mark = 0
ok = True
while i < len(s):
    if j < len(p) and (p[j] == '?' or p[j] == s[i]):
        i += 1
        j += 1
    elif j < len(p) and p[j] == '*':
        star = j
        mark = i
        j += 1
    elif star != -1:
        j = star + 1
        mark += 1
        i = mark
    else:
        ok = False
        break
if ok:
    while j < len(p) and p[j] == '*':
        j += 1
    ok = j == len(p)
print("YES" if ok else "NO")

title: Regular Expression Matching
description:
Implement simple regular-expression matching over the entire string s, where:

  • . matches any single character;
  • x* matches zero or more copies of the preceding element x (a letter or .);
  • any other character matches only itself.

Example: aab matches c*a*b (zero c, two a, one b); ab matches .*.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ |s|, |p| ≤ 200
  • s contains lowercase letters; p contains lowercase letters, . and *
  • Every * in p is preceded by a letter or . (no leading *, no **)
  • Naive recursion is exponential; use dynamic programming

Input

  • Line 1: the string s
  • Line 2: the pattern p

Output

YES if the pattern matches the whole string, otherwise NO.
